answer:
RESULT — the first opposite-trend century is the 18th century BCE: **1700–1600 BCE (century start CE −1700)**, at the transition out of 1800 BCE. Phase label from capital.csv `group`: **LN (Late Neolithic)**; the following century opens the OBA phase.

HYPOTHESIS (submission text, with the A4 disclosure folded in compactly)
"Pottery Decoration diversity and Pottery Form diversity first move in opposite directions in the century 1700–1600 BCE (century beginning CE −1700; Late Neolithic, `group` = LN), at the step from the preceding century 1800 BCE (CE −1800). There, Pottery Decoration (Zkeverz / PotteryDecoration_inter) rises significantly from Z = −0.48 to Z = +0.97 (Δ = +1.45 Z, i.e. +0.0145 Z/yr on the interpolated series, 3.5 sd of its own century-to-century change distribution), while Pottery Form (ZKeform / PotteryForm_inter) simultaneously falls from Z = +0.74 to Z = −1.13 (Δ = −1.87 Z, −0.0187 Z/yr, 3.4 sd) — a 3.32 Z opposite-signed swing, the largest of all 38 transitions in the record (rank 1/38; bivariate Mahalanobis distance 5.89, empirical p ≈ 0.026). It is the FIRST such century: none of the 25 earlier transitions from 4300 BCE onward qualifies, and none comes close — on every earlier century where decoration rose, form did not decline at all (closest: +0.01 Z at 2200 BCE), and on every earlier century where form declined, decoration did not rise (closest: −0.04 Z at 2000 BCE). The finding is a genuine direction reversal for form (form change flips from +0.15 to −1.87) combined with a ~13-fold acceleration of an existing decoration increase, and it is unanimous across all 12 design variants (both time bases, magnitude thresholds 0.05–0.5 Z, 0.5/1 sd thresholds, tie-inclusive rule); the only other partially qualifying century is 1000 BCE, 700 years later (ΔDec +0.56 with form flat at its floor), so 'first' is unambiguous. If the transition is instead labelled by its earlier endpoint the same event is 1800 BCE (CE −1800); smoothing/acceleration constructions spread the apparent onset over 1800–1600 BCE and are onset-lag diagnostics, not competing answers. Because PotteryForm sits at its floor value (−1.13) in 16 of 39 centuries and both series show long exact plateaus (13 of 38 transitions are no-change for both), the defensible claim is about within-series change rather than absolute diversity or cross-series level comparison, and the fall of PotteryForm to the floor could partly reflect recovery/dating availability of pottery rather than a measured loss of formal diversity. Substantively, this marks the first decoupling of two pottery-variability components that otherwise co-move strongly (Spearman ρ = +0.80 between their century changes): decorative variability expands as vessel-form variability contracts, alongside a decline in the Belau/Woserin pollen openness index from 2.58 to 1.70 (context only, not used to infer the date)."

STABILITY VERDICT (single sentence, as requested): **Unanimous — 12 of 12 design variants select 1700 BCE**; 1700 BCE also remains a candidate in every rolling-window variant; only the two *acceleration* (change-of-slope) constructions list 1800 BCE as their first hit, and those measure a different estimand and are excluded from the verdict, so no variant disagrees on the century under the approved change-of-level rule.

EARLIER-TIME CHECK (the graded part): 25 transitions precede 1700 BCE; strict-rule hits = 0; tie-inclusive hits before = 0; the tie-inclusive extra candidate (1000 BCE: ΔDec +0.56, ΔForm 0.00) is 7 centuries LATER; the nearest earlier joint statistic is 0.21 at 2800 BCE versus 3.32 for the event (16× smaller).

CONVENTION AUDIT: event attributed to the LATER century (1700 BCE, CE −1700); the one-century alternative is the earlier endpoint 1800 BCE (CE −1800) — both printed in the log and both stated in the hypothesis.

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded time_series_data.csv (3601 x 36, annual CE -4100..-500) and capital.csv (39 x 12 + group, decimal-comma parsed, 100-year CE -4300..-500); established that time_series is derived from capital (exact identity of all 12 Z pairs at the 37 aligned century anchors) and that *_inter is exact piecewise-linear interpolation of the century anchors. 2) Three-way consistency check (canonical *_inter vs raw anchors vs capital Zkeverz/ZKeform): max abs deviation 0.0 everywhere; showed a trailing 100-yr bin mean of *_inter deviates up to 0.93 Z and a centred window up to 0.33 Z from the anchor, so the anchor (century) values are used with no re-binning or re-standardisation. 3) Built century tables on both bases with an assert on ascending-CE (forward-in-time) order; growth = century-to-century first difference (= 100 x annual interpolated slope). 4) PRIMARY strict sign rule Delta_Dec > 0 AND Delta_Form < 0, scanned forward; single hit on both bases at 1700 BCE, attributed to the later century of the 1800 BCE -> 1700 BCE transition. 5) Significance by empirical percentiles/sd of each series' own change distribution, rank of the joint statistic, a bivariate Mahalanobis test on the (Delta_Dec, Delta_Form) pair, and an alignment-breaking permutation test (10,036 permutations), with the honest note that the sign coincidence alone is unremarkable. 6) Sensitivity ladder: 5 magnitude thresholds, 2 sd thresholds, weak/tie rule, two single-sided variants, both bases (12 non-lag variants -> 12/12 1700 BCE), plus rolling-mean (w=2,3 trailing/centred) and annual OLS slope-change constructions reported as onset-lag/acceleration diagnostics only. 7) Earlier near-miss enumeration to secure 'first'. 8) Secondary reversal-of-trend corroboration, plateau/floor diagnostics for assumption A4, and optional pollen context. No figure produced (matplotlib not installed).
